title: Dark Energy Report Review 2026: Intrigued by the AI Energy Pitch? What Altimetry's $129 Subscription Includes
excerpt: A closer look at the brand's AI power infrastructure theme, Hidden Alpha research bundle, and subscription terms-including renewal pricing and differing refund language.
content:
CAMBRIDGE, Mass., October 16, 2026 (Newswire.com) - Quick note: title phrases like "Dark Energy" and "$10 trillion" are Altimetry's own marketing language, not claims this publication has independently verified - see "The $10 Trillion Claim" section below for the full breakdown. This is also a paid advertorial, and a commission is earned if you buy through a link here. This content is promotional in nature, intended for consumer education about a commercially available product. It is not financial advice.

Company direct website: secure.altimetry.com. Details reflect brand materials reviewed in October 2026.

Explore the Hidden Alpha research package and introductory offer

Altimetry Hidden Alpha Reviews: Researching The $10 Trillion "Dark Energy" Pitch - and Reviewing What $129 Actually Buys (Consumer Research)

Hidden Alpha is Altimetry's stock-research subscription for self-directed investors who want individual-company research to supplement their own decisions - not a signal that any particular stock will rise. The introductory offer is $129 for the first year, with monthly issues, a model portfolio, and a themed bonus bundle the brand is calling "Dark Energy," covering AI-power-infrastructure plays alongside bonus reports on nuclear, AI stocks, and stocks to avoid; the brand states it renews at $199 annually, and that detail should be confirmed at checkout. Everything attributed to Altimetry below, including specific stock-return multiples and named-individual claims, is the brand's own claim-compared against available independent information where possible, and flagged plainly where it couldn't be confirmed.

You Saw an Ad

You saw an ad - maybe a video interview clip, maybe a headline about an energy technology tied to SpaceX, OpenAI, or a list of well-known tech names - and something about it stopped your scroll. Good instinct. Here's the short version: Hidden Alpha is Altimetry's flagship research newsletter, and the "Dark Energy" report is this cycle's big hook built around it. If you already research and pick your own stocks, the appeal is another source of company analysis to weigh alongside what you're already doing - here's exactly what that gets you, what it costs, and what's worth double-checking before you buy.

What Is Hidden Alpha and Who Is It For?

Hidden Alpha is positioned by Altimetry as an institutional-style equity research service, delivered monthly, aimed at self-directed investors who want stock ideas and sell signals without paying what Altimetry says its team charges institutional clients.

At a glance:

  • Delivery: 12 monthly issues plus bonus reports and a model portfolio
  • Built for: investors already comfortable picking individual stocks who want research to work alongside their own judgment
  • Not built for: a first-time investor looking for a hands-off, diversified portfolio
  • Risk to know upfront: Altimetry's own Terms of Use state plainly that recommended positions can lose value

What Is the Altimetry Dark Energy Report?

"Dark Energy" is Altimetry's promotional name for a bundled report included with a Hidden Alpha subscription-it's not a recognized industry or scientific category, so if you came here searching the physics term, this is an unrelated marketing label borrowed from it.

Here's what's actually confirmed about it:

  • Per the order page, the report is pitched as naming "key supplier stocks" tied to a broader AI-and-power infrastructure trend
  • A second bonus report covers small modular nuclear reactors
  • No specific stock names or tickers appear in the publicly accessible campaign materials reviewed for this article - so how many companies are covered or how the picks were selected can't be confirmed from the outside
  • If you're searching for a specific "Dark Energy stock ticker," none was identified in the publicly accessible campaign materials reviewed for this article

Buyer Takeaway: "Dark Energy" is a marketing label for a bundled report, not a confirmed stock ticker, a scientific finding, or an independently sized market. Treat the name as packaging-the question worth answering before buying is what's inside the report, not what the label implies.

The $10 Trillion Claim: What's Actually Behind It?

The order page makes two big claims. Here's each one, checked:

  • "A potential $10 trillion new technology" - the page doesn't cite a named study, government estimate, or market-research firm; it reads like Altimetry's own framing of a market opportunity. General web searches run for this article in October 2026 did not surface an independent market-size report corroborating the figure. That search wasn't exhaustive, and a result not turning up isn't proof the figure appears nowhere - but no such source turned up in the searches actually performed.
  • The White House "greenlit the underlying technology... on an emergency basis" - similarly unsourced on the page; the same October 2026 searches didn't turn up an independent government announcement matching that description.

Treat both as unverified brand marketing language, not researched market data, until Altimetry - or an independent source - publishes the underlying basis for them.

Are Major Technology Executives Actually Involved?

The order page names four well-known names as "early backers" of the broader trend behind the Dark Energy report:

  • Elon Musk
  • Sam Altman
  • Jensen Huang
  • Larry Ellison

It also states the underlying technology is "critical to the operations of SpaceX, OpenAI, Google, Microsoft, Meta, Amazon, Oracle."

Here's the real picture:

  • What's widely reported: AI-industry companies in general are pursuing new power-generation capacity to meet data-center demand - a real, well-documented trend
  • What this article did not find: independent confirmation that these four individuals are personally "early backers" of whatever specific technology or stocks the Dark Energy report covers, as opposed to their companies' broader, publicly known interest in energy for AI infrastructure
  • What was located: no endorsement by any of these four individuals of Altimetry, Hidden Alpha, or this specific report

Treat the names as part of Altimetry's marketing narrative connecting a real industry trend to its product, not as confirmation that any of these executives are personally involved with, aware of, or endorsing this subscription.

What Does the Subscription Actually Include?

Per the brand's order page, here's what you actually get in the welcome package Altimetry values at $1,794:

  • 12 monthly issues of Hidden Alpha ($499 brand-stated value)
  • The "Dark Energy" themed report naming supplier stocks Altimetry ties to the trend ($299 brand-stated value)
  • A bonus report on small modular nuclear reactors ($199 brand-stated value)
  • A bonus report on AI-related stocks ($299 brand-stated value)
  • A bonus report listing stocks Altimetry recommends avoiding ($299 brand-stated value)
  • Year-round access to the Hidden Alpha model portfolio and email updates
  • A bonus video briefing and a second bonus interview segment
  • One free year of a second Altimetry publication, the Timetable Investor ($199 brand-stated value)
  • Access to "The Altimeter," described as Altimetry's stock-grading database
  • A digital archive of past issues
  • A companion publication called Money & Megatrends
  • A complimentary one-year membership to TradeStops Basic, a separate product from TradeSmith ($299 brand-stated value), opt-outable at checkout

Here's how the "$1,794" welcome-package math actually breaks down:

  • What adds up to $1,794: six items carry a brand-stated dollar value - Hidden Alpha ($499), the Dark Energy report ($299), the nuclear report ($199), the AI report ($299), the stocks-to-avoid report ($299), and the Timetable Investor subscription ($199)
  • What's included but not priced: model-portfolio access, the bonus video and interview segment, Altimeter database access, the digital archive, and Money & Megatrends - all carry no separately stated dollar value on the order page
  • What's separate from the $1,794 figure entirely: TradeStops Basic, listed with its own brand-stated $299 value

All of these numbers are Altimetry's own promotional valuations, not independently appraised or audited prices.

What Do the Historical Stock-Return Examples Actually Show?

Altimetry's promotional materials reference historical gains tied to three real, publicly traded semiconductor-equipment companies: Lam Research, KLA, and Applied Materials.

A few things worth knowing before those names get you excited:

  • These are not performance results for Hidden Alpha's current recommendations - they describe what happened to unrelated, already-public companies at some point in the past
  • They're not a projection or guarantee for whatever stocks the Dark Energy report itself names
  • The materials reviewed for this article don't establish the calculation periods or methodology behind the brand's cited outcomes, so this article doesn't repeat the specific dollar multiples Altimetry uses to illustrate them
  • Past performance doesn't guarantee future results, and Altimetry's own Terms of Use state plainly that it doesn't guarantee investment results and that recommended positions can lose value

Buyer Takeaway: Read the historical examples as marketing context about a category - semiconductor-equipment suppliers tied to major industry buildouts - not as evidence about what the Dark Energy report's specific, still-undisclosed picks will do. Ask Altimetry directly for the timeframe and methodology behind any multiplier figure in the ad before treating it as a benchmark.

Pricing: What the Order Page and Terms of Use Say

Here's what you'll actually pay, per Altimetry's own order page and Terms of Use, reviewed in October 2026:

  • Introductory price: $129 for the first year (regular price listed as $499; the "$370 today's discount" figure is Altimetry's own reference-point framing, not an independently verified market price).
  • Auto-renewal: the subscription renews automatically at $199 per year (plus applicable taxes) unless the subscriber gives notice of non-renewal at least one day before the renewal date.
  • Non-renewal notice: per Terms of Use §7(B), by calling 1-800-701-9346 (Mon-Fri, 9 a.m.-5 p.m. ET), by emailing contactus@altimetry.com, or by another method Altimetry designates - at least one day before the renewal date.
  • Formal subscription cancellation: per Terms of Use §7(C), the Premium Services cancellation clause names phone (1-800-701-9346) or "any other designated cancellation method," and states a subscriber "may not cancel a subscription by any other means" - the Terms do not explicitly confirm whether email qualifies as a designated method for this specific clause, separately from the email option named for non-renewal notice above.
  • Email: contact@altimetry.com (general inquiries, per the Privacy Policy) and contactus@altimetry.com (named for non-renewal notice and other cancellations, per the Terms of Use).

Check the current price, renewal terms, and refund conditions

What the Sales Page Says vs. What the Terms of Use Say About Refunds

This gets its own section because the two documents don't fully match:

  • Order page: "100% Money-Back Guarantee. Take the next 30 days to try out Hidden Alpha. If you're unhappy for any reason, simply contact our member services team within the first 30 days and you'll receive a full refund."
  • Terms of Use, Section 7(C): once the initial subscription begins, Altimetry states it generally does not refund initial orders or recurring monthly payments. For a subscription term longer than a month - which an annual plan is - canceled within the first 30 days, the subscriber "may receive a refund of your subscription fee minus the equivalent of one-month pro-rated charge," not the full amount the order page implies. After the first 30 days, no refund is given regardless of usage.

These two statements haven't been reconciled by Altimetry for this specific offer: the promotional page describes a 30-day full-refund guarantee, while the general Terms of Use describe a potentially prorated refund for annual subscriptions canceled within 30 days. This article doesn't clarify which one governs your specific purchase-before you rely on either version, get written confirmation of the applicable offer-specific refund terms from Altimetry's member services team.

Review the official guarantee terms before ordering

Who Writes Hidden Alpha?

Two names are behind the research, and here's what's actually confirmed about each:

  • Joel Litman - named on the order page as Altimetry's Chief Investment Officer and the voice behind Hidden Alpha. DePaul University's faculty directory, independent of Altimetry, lists him as a Certified Public Accountant (Illinois) with an MBA/MM from Northwestern's Kellogg School of Management and a BS in Accountancy from DePaul.
  • Rob Spivey - named on Altimetry's order page as director of research. MarketWise's own company bio page lists him as "Rob Spivey, CFA," a CFA charterholder and CFA Institute member. Because MarketWise is Altimetry's parent company, that's the credential Altimetry's corporate family claims for him-not an independent third-party audit.

A separate third-party review (thestockdork.com) reports the same two credentials.

Is Hidden Alpha Right for You?

  • Likely a good fit if: you already invest in individual stocks and want a research service to supplement your own due diligence, not replace it
  • Likely not a fit if: you're looking for personalized financial planning (Altimetry explicitly states it doesn't provide this) or want a hands-off investment solution
  • Worth weighing either way: the subscription renews automatically at a higher price next year unless you provide timely nonrenewal notice through an accepted method - if that's a dealbreaker for you, mark your renewal date now

Company and Contact Information

If you need to reach Altimetry directly - to confirm a refund, verify a cancellation, or ask a question the order page doesn't answer - here's what's publicly listed. Altimetry is operated by VRSH, LLC, which the Privacy Policy and Terms of Use identify as "a MarketWise company." Two addresses appear in the brand's own materials, and both are documented here rather than silently picking one:

  • Operating entity: VRSH, LLC, d/b/a Altimetry, a MarketWise company
  • Correspondence/privacy address (per Privacy Policy): 110 Cambridge St., Cambridge, MA 02141
  • Phone: 1-800-701-9346 (Mon-Fri, 9 a.m.-5 p.m. ET)
  • Email: contact@altimetry.com

Fast Facts

  • Product: Hidden Alpha, monthly equity research newsletter plus bonus reports
  • Publisher: Altimetry (VRSH, LLC), a MarketWise company
  • Introductory price: $129 for year one
  • Renewal price: $199/year, auto-renewing
  • Non-renewal notice: phone or email, at least 1 day before renewal; formal cancellation: phone or another designated method (see Pricing section for the email nuance)
  • Stated guarantee: 30-day money-back per the order page; Terms of Use describe a pro-rated refund within 30 days, not a full refund
  • Bundle value claimed: $1,794 (brand-stated)
  • Included bonus product: TradeStops Basic (1 year), opt-out available at checkout, separate company (TradeSmith)
  • Regulatory status: publisher of financial information; not a registered investment adviser, per Altimetry's own Terms of Use
  • Lead editor named: Joel Litman, Chief Investment Officer, Altimetry
  • Director of research named: Rob Spivey

Frequently Asked Questions

Is Hidden Alpha personalized investment advice?

No, and that's an important distinction to keep in mind before you subscribe. Altimetry's Terms of Use state explicitly that the service relies on the publisher's exclusion from the definition of investment adviser, that its content is impersonal and not tailored to any individual subscriber's financial situation, goals, or risk tolerance, and that Altimetry's own representatives will not provide you personalized investment advice even if you contact them directly. That's Altimetry's own characterization of its regulatory status, not an independent legal determination by this article - whether a publisher actually qualifies for that exclusion depends on factors like how it's circulated and whether its timing is tied to specific trades, which this article did not separately audit. In practice, what it means for you day to day is that you're getting general research and commentary you apply to your own decisions - not a recommendation built around your specific portfolio.

How much does Hidden Alpha cost after the first year?

Per the order page and Terms of Use, you pay $129 for the introductory year, and the subscription then renews automatically at $199 per year unless you give notice of non-renewal at least one day before your renewal date. You can do that by phone, by email, or by another method Altimetry designates. That's a meaningful jump from the introductory price - roughly 54% higher - so mark your renewal date if you want to make an active decision about whether to keep the subscription rather than let it renew by default.

Does Altimetry guarantee the stocks in the Dark Energy report will perform as described?

No, and you shouldn't treat anything in the marketing campaign as a guarantee of future results. Altimetry's own Terms of Use state plainly that it does not guarantee investment results, returns, or performance of any kind, and that trading in securities involves risk and volatility - including the risk that any position you buy based on its recommendations loses value after you purchase it. That standard disclaimer applies to the Dark Energy picks exactly as it applies to every other recommendation Altimetry publishes.

Who are Elon Musk, Sam Altman, and the other names mentioned in the ad?

They're named on Altimetry's order page as "early backers" of the broader energy trend the Dark Energy report covers - real, well-known technology executives whose companies are, in general, publicly reported to be pursuing new energy capacity for AI infrastructure. What you should know before you let that lend the pitch credibility: this article did not locate independent confirmation that these specific individuals are personally backing whatever technology or stocks the report names, and none of them has been found to have endorsed Altimetry, Hidden Alpha, or this report. Treat the names as part of the marketing narrative, not as a personal endorsement.

How do I cancel if I don't want the subscription to renew?

To stop the subscription from auto-renewing, the Terms of Use state notice must be given at least one day before the renewal date - by phone (1-800-701-9346, Mon-Fri, 9 a.m.-5 p.m. ET), by emailing contactus@altimetry.com, or by another method Altimetry designates. A separate clause covering formal Premium Services cancellation names phone or "any other designated cancellation method" without explicitly listing email for that specific step - when in doubt, call and request written confirmation of the cancellation.

Is there a specific "Dark Energy" stock ticker Altimetry has identified?

No specific ticker was identified in the public campaign materials reviewed for this article. Altimetry's order page references unnamed "key supplier stocks" and says more are named inside the actual report, but no specific company name or ticker symbol is published anywhere on the publicly accessible order page itself - only the promise that the information is inside. If you see a specific ticker attributed to Altimetry's Dark Energy report somewhere other than the paid product, that's worth double-checking against the brand's own materials before you act on it, since this article found nothing to confirm it independently.

Is Altimetry Hidden Alpha legitimate, or is it a scam?

Altimetry identifies VRSH, LLC as the operating entity behind the service and publishes Terms of Use, a correspondence address, and customer-service contact information. Those details help a reader identify who they'd actually be doing business with - but they don't, by themselves, establish that the Dark Energy campaign's specific claims (the $10 trillion figure, the named-executive framing, the historical stock-return examples) are accurate. The materials reviewed for this article do not establish whether every promotional representation in the campaign is accurate. The two questions - is this a real, identifiable company, and are its marketing claims independently verified - are separate, and this article only answers the first one with confidence.

Bottom Line

Hidden Alpha is a financial research subscription offered by Altimetry, which identifies VRSH, LLC as its operating entity and describes itself as a MarketWise company. Its promotional campaign for this cycle emphasizes a "Dark Energy" investment theme, historical stock-market examples drawn from unrelated public companies, and references to well-known technology executives. Those marketing claims should be evaluated separately from the publisher's corporate identity and the subscription features actually described in its materials - the product itself (monthly research, a model portfolio, bonus reports, and support access) is clearly laid out in the brand's own materials, independent of how the campaign around it is framed. Before you pay, confirm two things directly with Altimetry: (1) which refund terms actually apply if you cancel within 30 days, since the order page and the Terms of Use describe different outcomes, and (2) the specific factual basis for the "Dark Energy" trend claims, since those aren't independently verified here. If you want research-service-style content without the hard-sell framing, it's worth comparing a few providers before you commit to an annual plan that renews on its own.

Material Limitations

This article is based on Altimetry's own order page, Terms of Use, and Privacy Policy as supplied for this release, and on a live check of the affiliate link. No product testing or independent investment-performance analysis was performed. Brand claims about the underlying "Dark Energy" technology, named-individual involvement, and historical stock multiples are not independently verified and are presented as brand-stated. The refund-terms discrepancy between the order page and Section 7(C) of the Terms of Use is documented above rather than resolved; contact Altimetry directly to confirm which applies to your specific plan and timing.

Third-Party Feedback Platforms

No third-party review-platform ratings were cited in this article. Where such ratings appear elsewhere, their accuracy is not endorsed here and should be evaluated critically.

Forward-Looking Statements

This article reflects Altimetry materials reviewed in October 2026. Pricing, bundle contents, guarantee terms, and contact details may change. Rely on Altimetry's official order page and current Terms of Use for up-to-date information before purchasing.

Marketing Language Notice

Attribution language throughout this article identifies statements originating with the brand. Title and order-page phrases such as "Dark Energy" and "$10 trillion new technology" are Altimetry's own promotional language, not independent rankings, lab results, or verified claims by this publication.

Geographic and Jurisdiction Notice

Altimetry's Terms of Use state the service is directed to individuals and entities residing in the United States, that the agreement is governed by Maryland law, and that disputes are to be brought in a federal or state court in Baltimore County, Maryland.

Trademark Acknowledgment

"Altimetry," "Hidden Alpha," and related marks are the property of VRSH, LLC and/or its affiliates. "TradeStops" and "TradeSmith" are the property of their respective owner and are a separate company from Altimetry. All other trademarks referenced belong to their respective owners.
